hotspots.topic: Wind load basics for sign structures
hotspots.whyItMatters: Sign structural failures are almost always a wind-load problem — the exam tests whether you know load matters, not the calc itself.
hotspots.cite: Engineering Sign Structures — confirm chapter in your copy
hotspots.trap: Sizing a sign's electrical/structural support for its weight alone and ignoring lateral wind loading.

hotspots.whyItMatters: Freestanding sign poles rely on footing depth and soil bearing — a recurring structural/electrical crossover topic.
hotspots.cite: Engineering Sign Structures — confirm chapter in your copy
hotspots.trap: Using one fixed embedment depth regardless of pole height, sign area, or local soil conditions.

hotspots.topic: Attachment and bracing of sign faces
hotspots.whyItMatters: Connects the sign's structural support to the electrical raceway/enclosure mounted on it.
hotspots.cite: Engineering Sign Structures — confirm chapter in your copy
hotspots.trap: Assuming the electrical enclosure's mounting hardware also satisfies the structural bracing requirement for the sign face.
